patient.name: Rukhsana Miah
patient.setting: GP surgery, then metabolic bone clinic
patient.complaint: Six months of aching bones and difficulty climbing stairs
background: Bangladeshi heritage; covers her skin outdoors
Works indoors as a pharmacy dispenser in Tower Hamlets

diagnosis.exam: Expect 'Which is the most likely diagnosis?' with diffuse bone pain, proximal weakness and a bone profile of low calcium and phosphate with raised ALP and PTH.

points: Rukhsana, 39, pharmacy dispenser in Tower Hamlets, Bangladeshi heritage.
Six months of **aching bones**: hips, ribs, lower back.
Struggles to **climb stairs** and get up from a chair.
Covers her skin outdoors; mostly indoors at work.

steps.lead: Rukhsana's bones are **soft**, not thin: the matrix is there but not mineralised, so they ache and can bend or break.
Little sun exposure and **darker skin** are Rukhsana's risk factors. Also ask about coeliac disease, CKD and anticonvulsants.

points: Tender over the ribs and tibiae when pressed.
Rises from a chair using her arms.

steps.lead: Diffuse symmetrical aches, **proximal weakness** and a waddling gait: the usual insidious picture.

steps.q: Which feature best separates Rukhsana's osteomalacia from osteoporosis?
steps.r: Osteoporosis is **painless** until it fractures. Pain, tenderness and proximal myopathy point to osteomalacia.

steps.lead: The signature triad: **diffuse bone pain, proximal muscle weakness, raised ALP**. Rukhsana has the first two; bloods will show the third.

steps.text: Do not label proximal weakness in a young woman as 'just polymyalgia' or 'just tiredness'. Check **vitamin D and ALP**.

investigation.exam: Expect the bloods pattern (low vitamin D, calcium, phosphate; high ALP and PTH) and the X-ray finding (Looser's zones).

steps.title: Bone profile and vitamin D
steps.text: Low calcium, phosphate and vitamin D with high ALP and PTH. Coeliac screen negative.

steps.lead: Rukhsana's diagnosis is **biochemical** with supportive imaging: low vitamin D, calcium and phosphate, high ALP and a high PTH (secondary).

steps.r: Low calcium drives **secondary hyperparathyroidism**. A primary adenoma would give a **high** calcium.

visual.title: ALP
visual.label: Rukhsana 286
visual.caption: High osteoblast activity trying to build bone: **raised ALP** completes the triad.

steps.lead: Rukhsana's pelvic X-ray shows **Looser's zones**: thin radiolucent lines with sclerotic borders across the femoral necks.

steps.text: Looser's zones (pseudofractures) are the X-ray buzzword. Lucent transverse bands, sclerotic edges, classically at the **hip**, pubic rami and ribs.

management.exam: Expect first-line treatment (high-dose vitamin D loading, calcium if needed) and maintenance dosing; bisphosphonates are the distractor.

steps.r: Replace what is missing: **high-dose colecalciferol** loading, with calcium if deficient. Bisphosphonates treat osteoporosis.

steps.lead: Rukhsana starts a **colecalciferol** loading course with calcium, and the cause (low sunlight, covering) is addressed.

steps.text: Do not start a **bisphosphonate** before replacing vitamin D. In osteomalacia it can drop calcium further and does not fix mineralisation.

steps.lead: If Rukhsana's calcium were very low with **tetany or seizures**, she would need urgent correction (IV calcium) before oral loading.

visual.title: Rukhsana's response
visual.caption: Vitamin D rises fast; ALP falls slowly as bone remineralises, and her pain eases.

steps.lead: Rukhsana then takes **400–800 IU daily** maintenance, with sunlight and dietary advice to stop it recurring.

steps.title: Managing osteomalacia
nodes: Severe hypocalcaemia with tetany or seizures → urgent IV correction
Treat cause: malabsorption, CKD, diet, drugs
Recheck calcium, ALP and vitamin D

science.exam: Expect mechanisms: unmineralised osteoid, why PTH and ALP rise, why muscles are weak, or the child equivalent (rickets).

steps.lead: Rukhsana's low vitamin D cuts gut **calcium and phosphate** absorption, so osteoid cannot be mineralised with **hydroxyapatite**.

steps.title: From low vitamin D to soft bones
nodes: Less gut calcium and phosphate absorption
Excess unmineralised osteoid: soft, painful bone

steps.lead: Rukhsana's high PTH is **compensatory**: it pulls calcium from bone, raising ALP and wasting phosphate in the urine.
Skeletal muscle has **vitamin D receptors**; Rukhsana's deficiency weakens her hip and shoulder muscles.
Rukhsana's Looser's zones are patches of **unmineralised osteoid** where stress is highest, such as the femoral neck.

steps.q: Rukhsana's 6 year old nephew has bowed legs and the same bloods. What is his condition called?
steps.r: Defective mineralisation **before epiphyseal fusion** is **rickets**; after fusion it is osteomalacia.

steps.lead: The child version, before the growth plates fuse, is **rickets**: bowed legs and widened wrists.

o: Excess bone resorption with normal mineral
Reduced bone mass with normal mineralisation
mcq.r: **Defective mineralisation**; reduced mass with normal mineral is osteoporosis.

prompts.q: What is osteomalacia and what is its commonest cause?

points.p: Soft, weak bones: pain, fracture, deformity (bowing)

prompts.q: Who gets osteomalacia? List the risk factors.
prompts.tip: Exam thinking: stem hides it in lifestyle or drugs.

prompts.q: How does osteomalacia present, and what is the signature triad?

points.p: Diffuse symmetrical bone pain and tenderness
Proximal muscle weakness, difficulty with stairs/chairs
Triad: bone pain, proximal weakness, raised ALP

prompts.q: How do you tell osteomalacia from osteoporosis and primary hyperparathyroidism?

points.p: Osteoporosis: normal bloods, painless until fracture

points.why: Osteomalacia has low or normal calcium.

prompts.q: What does the X-ray show in osteomalacia?

points.p: Radiolucent transverse lines with sclerotic border

prompts.q: What is first-line and long-term treatment of osteomalacia?

points.p: Treat the cause: malabsorption, CKD, diet
Maintenance 400–800 IU daily, sunlight and diet advice

prompts.q: When is osteomalacia an emergency and what do you do?
prompts.tip: Exam thinking: tetany changes the route.

prompts.q: What is the pathophysiology of osteomalacia, and why does PTH rise?

points.p: Low vitamin D reduces gut calcium and phosphate absorption
Impaired hydroxyapatite deposition: excess unmineralised osteoid
Secondary hyperparathyroidism compensates for low calcium, raising ALP

prompts.q: Why are muscles weak, why do Looser's zones form, and what is the child equivalent?

points.p: Vitamin D receptors in skeletal muscle; deficiency impairs function
Looser's zones: unmineralised osteoid at stress sites
Rickets in children before epiphyseal fusion

glossary.osteomalacia: Soft bones in adults from defective mineralisation, usually due to vitamin D deficiency.
glossary.rickets: Defective mineralisation in children before the growth plates fuse.
glossary.osteoid: The protein matrix of bone, laid down before it is mineralised.
glossary.hydroxyapatite: The calcium phosphate crystal that hardens bone.
glossary.mineralisation: Deposition of calcium phosphate into the bone matrix.
glossary.osteoporosis: Low bone mass with normal mineral and normal blood tests.
glossary.ALP: Alkaline phosphatase; rises with high bone-building activity.
glossary.PTH: Parathyroid hormone; rises in osteomalacia to compensate for low calcium.
glossary.secondary hyperparathyroidism: Raised PTH as an appropriate response to low calcium.
glossary.25-OH vitamin D: 25-hydroxyvitamin D, the storage form measured to assess vitamin D status.
glossary.25-hydroxyvitamin D: The storage form of vitamin D measured in blood.
glossary.colecalciferol: Vitamin D3, used for loading and maintenance replacement.
glossary.IU: International units, used to dose vitamin D.
glossary.Looser's zones: Pseudofractures: radiolucent transverse bands with sclerotic edges, often at the hip.
glossary.pseudofractures: Bands of unmineralised bone that look like incomplete fractures on X-ray.
glossary.radiolucent: Appearing dark on X-ray because it lets X-rays through.
glossary.sclerotic: Denser than normal bone; white on X-ray.
glossary.proximal muscle weakness: Weakness of muscles near the trunk, such as the hips and shoulders.
glossary.proximal myopathy: Disease of the muscles of the hips and shoulders causing weakness.
glossary.waddling gait: Side-to-side walk from weak hip muscles.
glossary.insufficiency fracture: A fracture of weakened bone under normal stress.
glossary.coeliac disease: Immune reaction to gluten damaging the small bowel and causing malabsorption.
glossary.malabsorption: Poor absorption of nutrients from the gut.
glossary.tissue transglutaminase: Antibody test (tTG IgA) used to screen for coeliac disease.
glossary.anticonvulsants: Anti-seizure drugs; some speed up vitamin D breakdown.
glossary.phenytoin: An enzyme-inducing anticonvulsant linked to osteomalacia.
glossary.CKD: Chronic kidney disease; reduces vitamin D activation.
glossary.epiphyseal fusion: Closure of the growth plates at the end of growth.
glossary.tetany: Involuntary muscle spasm from low calcium.
glossary.carpopedal spasm: Spasm of the hands and feet from low calcium.
glossary.calcium gluconate: IV calcium used urgently for symptomatic hypocalcaemia.
glossary.DEXA: Bone density scan; cannot tell osteomalacia from osteoporosis.
glossary.bisphosphonates: Drugs that block osteoclasts; for osteoporosis, not first-line in osteomalacia.
glossary.Paget's disease: Disordered bone remodelling with very high ALP but normal calcium and phosphate.
glossary.creatine kinase: Muscle enzyme; high in myositis, normal in osteomalacia myopathy.

technique.stem: A 42 year old woman has 6 months of aching in her hips, back and ribs and difficulty climbing stairs. She rarely goes outside. She walks with a waddling gait. Investigations: adjusted calcium 2.10 mmol/L (2.20–2.60), phosphate 0.66 mmol/L (0.80–1.50), ALP 248 IU/L (30–130), PTH 13.2 pmol/L (1.6–8.5).
technique.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

steps.x: Diagnosis from bone pain plus bloods.

clues: aching in her hips, back and ribs
steps.x: Bone pain, proximal weakness, low sun; low calcium and phosphate, high ALP and PTH.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Raised ALP alone with normal calcium and phosphate.
Proximal weakness with high CK, not bone chemistry changes.

steps.x: **B. Osteomalacia.** Pain + proximal weakness + raised ALP = osteomalacia.

technique.stem: A 55 year old man with coeliac disease has bone pain and proximal weakness. His bone profile shows low calcium and phosphate with a raised ALP. An X-ray of the pelvis is taken.
technique.q: Which is the most likely finding on the pelvic X-ray?

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

steps.x: **C. Looser's zones.** Osteomalacia X-ray: Looser's zones at the hip.

technique.stem: A 36 year old woman has osteomalacia due to dietary vitamin D deficiency. Investigations: adjusted calcium 2.12 mmol/L (2.20–2.60), 25-OH vitamin D 14 nmol/L (>50), ALP 210 IU/L (30–130). She has no tetany and her ECG is normal.
technique.q: Which is the most appropriate initial management?
o: Low-dose vitamin D 400 IU daily only

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: For osteoporosis; not a mineralisation fix.
PTH is high only as compensation.

steps.x: **D. Oral colecalciferol loading dose.** Load first, then maintain.

technique.stem: A 40 year old woman has osteomalacia. A bone biopsy is taken from the iliac crest.
technique.q: Which is the most likely histological finding?

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

steps.x: **A. Excess unmineralised osteoid.** Osteomalacia: matrix is there, mineral is not.

practice.stem: A 44 year old woman of Somali heritage has 8 months of diffuse bone pain and difficulty rising from a chair. Her pulse rate is 74 bpm, BP 116/70 mmHg and temperature 36.8°C. Investigations are shown.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Bone pain, proximal weakness and low calcium, phosphate and vitamin D with raised ALP and PTH is osteomalacia. Osteoporosis has normal bloods.

steps.x: Dark skin, bone pain, proximal weakness; classic bloods.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

steps.x: **B. Osteomalacia.** Low calcium + low phosphate + high ALP + high PTH = osteomalacia.

practice.stem: A 50 year old man has hip pain and proximal weakness. His pulse rate is 72 bpm and BP 128/80 mmHg. Bloods show low calcium, low phosphate and a raised ALP. A pelvic X-ray is taken.
practice.q: Which is the most likely finding on the X-ray?
o: Bilateral transverse lucent bands with sclerotic margins
practice.e: Looser's zones are radiolucent transverse bands with sclerotic borders, classically at the hip. Punched-out lesions are myeloma.

clues: low calcium, low phosphate and a raised ALP

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Looser's zones**: lucent bands with sclerotic borders.
**A. Bilateral transverse lucent bands with sclerotic margins.** Pseudofractures at the hip.

practice.stem: A 33 year old woman has bone pain, bloating and loose, pale stools for a year. She has iron deficiency anaemia. Her pulse rate is 78 bpm and BP 112/70 mmHg. Bloods show low calcium, low phosphate, raised ALP and low vitamin D.
practice.q: Which is the most likely underlying cause of her osteomalacia?
practice.e: Steatorrhoea with iron and vitamin D deficiency points to coeliac malabsorption as the cause.

steps.x: Malabsorption with iron and vitamin D deficiency.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Renal function would be abnormal; no GI clue.
Does not explain malabsorption or iron deficiency.

steps.x: **B. Coeliac disease.** Osteomalacia + GI symptoms + iron deficiency: coeliac.

practice.stem: A 46 year old man with epilepsy has taken phenytoin for 20 years. He now has bone pain and a waddling gait. His pulse rate is 70 bpm and BP 124/78 mmHg. Investigations are shown.
practice.q: Which is the most likely cause of his bone disease?
practice.e: Enzyme-inducing anticonvulsants such as phenytoin increase vitamin D breakdown and cause osteomalacia.

clues: bone pain and a waddling gait

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

steps.x: **A. Anticonvulsant-induced vitamin D deficiency.** Anticonvulsants are a classic cause.

practice.stem: A 38 year old woman with vitamin D deficiency has had aching bones for months. Her pulse rate is 76 bpm and BP 118/74 mmHg. She is asked to stand from a squat and walk across the room.
practice.q: Which is the most likely finding on examination?
practice.e: Proximal muscle weakness in osteomalacia causes a waddling gait and difficulty rising from a squat.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

steps.x: **E. Waddling gait.** Proximal weakness: waddling gait, difficulty rising.

practice.stem: A 70 year old woman has non-specific muscle and bone pain. She fractured her wrist after a minor fall 2 months ago and is housebound. Her pulse rate is 80 bpm and BP 132/80 mmHg. Investigations are shown.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Low calcium and phosphate with raised ALP and PTH in a housebound woman is osteomalacia from vitamin D deficiency.

steps.x: Housebound, fracture, bone pain; low calcium and phosphate, high ALP and PTH.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

steps.x: **C. Osteomalacia.** Low phosphate separates it from pseudohypoparathyroidism.

practice.stem: A 41 year old woman has diffuse bone pain and proximal weakness. Her pulse rate is 74 bpm and BP 120/76 mmHg. Bone profile shows low calcium, low phosphate and a raised ALP.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the cause?
practice.e: Low 25-hydroxyvitamin D confirms deficiency as the cause; DEXA shows low density but cannot tell osteomalacia from osteoporosis.

clues: diffuse bone pain and proximal weakness
low calcium, low phosphate and a raised ALP

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

steps.x: **C. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D.** Osteomalacia: measure vitamin D.

practice.stem: A 48 year old man has low calcium, low phosphate, raised ALP and low vitamin D. His pulse rate is 72 bpm and BP 126/80 mmHg. He has groin pain on walking.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate imaging?
practice.e: A plain pelvic X-ray shows Looser's zones (pseudofractures), classically at the hip.

clues: raised ALP and low vitamin D

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

steps.x: **D. Plain X-ray of the pelvis.** X-ray shows pseudofractures.

practice.stem: A 35 year old woman has osteomalacia due to poor sunlight exposure. Her pulse rate is 70 bpm and BP 114/72 mmHg. She has no tetany. 25-OH vitamin D is 13 nmol/L (>50) and calcium 2.14 mmol/L (2.20–2.60).
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate initial management?
practice.e: First-line treatment is high-dose vitamin D loading with calcium if deficient; bisphosphonates do not correct mineralisation.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

steps.x: **C. High-dose colecalciferol loading.** Load vitamin D first.

practice.stem: A 40 year old woman with osteomalacia has completed a vitamin D loading course. Her pulse rate is 72 bpm and BP 118/72 mmHg. Vitamin D is now 78 nmol/L (>50) and ALP is falling.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate long-term management?
practice.e: After loading, low-dose maintenance vitamin D (400–800 IU daily) with lifestyle advice prevents recurrence.

clues: completed a vitamin D loading course

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

steps.x: **E. Vitamin D 800 IU daily.** Load, then maintain.

practice.stem: A 29 year old woman with severe osteomalacia has carpopedal spasm and tingling of her lips. Her pulse rate is 104 bpm and BP 120/76 mmHg. Adjusted calcium is 1.62 mmol/L (2.20–2.60).
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate initial management?
practice.e: Severe hypocalcaemia with tetany needs urgent correction with IV calcium gluconate before vitamin D replacement.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

steps.x: **B. IV calcium gluconate.** Tetany: urgent IV correction first.

practice.stem: A 45 year old woman has osteomalacia with proximal muscle weakness. Her pulse rate is 76 bpm and BP 122/78 mmHg. Creatine kinase is normal.
practice.q: Which is the most likely mechanism of her weakness?
o: Vitamin D receptor deficiency in muscle
practice.e: Skeletal muscle has vitamin D receptors; deficiency impairs muscle protein synthesis and function.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Low **vitamin D receptor** signalling impairs muscle.
**E. Vitamin D receptor deficiency in muscle.** Vitamin D acts directly on muscle.
